expectedRealization.rationale: Financing relief can affect survival/cost of capital over quarters, but no coherent company subset with a frozen earnings bridge is identified.

changeHypothesis.summary: Central policy explicitly intensified tax and financing support for private firms under stress, but the beneficiaries are heterogeneous and depend on leverage, pledge risk and viable business economics.
changeHypothesis.persistenceReason: Policy support can persist for quarters, but transmission varies sharply by firm quality and balance sheet.
disconfirmingEvidence: Broad support does not distinguish viable firms from structurally weak firms.
No frozen candidate set with direct financing-cost-to-earnings conversion was established.

selectionComparison.rationale: No selection: the event is too broad and company transmission is unresolved.

expectations.marketExpectationAtCutoff: Policy support is public and broad; distressed private-company beta is not a valid substitute for company-specific earnings transmission.
expectations.thesisExpectation: Require a coherent subset with measured financing-cost/survival/earnings benefit.
expectations.measurableGap: No such frozen subset is available.

hypothesisDecompositionTest.rationale: Beneficiary quality, leverage and pledge risk must be decomposed before selection.

nearTerm.driver: policy signaling can ease financing sentiment before actual earnings transmission

mediumTerm.driver: financing access may improve for viable firms but not all distressed firms

structural.driver: lower financing/tax burden can support private-sector health

evidenceHorizonMatrix.resolutionRule: Split by balance sheet/business quality and measure direct financing-to-earnings transmission before selection.

bearCase: Relief improves sentiment but weak firms remain weak and equity-pledge problems persist.
nextResearchActions: No selection; future discovery may create narrower financing-relief hypotheses only with company-level evidence.
